nodes.label: ACQUIRE / SETTLE / REC take phases (height band 18-28 cm, palm within 40 degrees, >= 90% coverage on one hand id)

nodes.label: Live warm-up per hand: ACQUIRE, OPEN PALM 4 s, FIST 4 s (an initial calibration, not the offline learning)
nodes.author: Nicholas Kim
nodes.rationale: The open palm gives the glove's rails, the camera's open reference and the bone-length frames; the fist gives both flexed ends. A hand is refused when ACQUIRE times out, the camera did not see the open palm, or the index span is under 0.40 (glove) or 0.30 (camera). Eight seconds is a far smaller sample than a session, so replay, repeat the warm-up across don/doff and days, and check the lag's sign before trusting live output.

nodes.label: leap_hand.pose_check: a take whose hand is not in the called pose is refused (two-sensor rule)
nodes.author: Nicholas Kim

A finger is only wrong when BOTH sensors are decisive and BOTH contradict the pose. Pinch is judged on the camera's thumb-index gap alone (pinch_camera_gap) and never rejected on; an edge-on camera (median view angle over 65 degrees) casts no vote.

nodes.author: Nicholas Kim
nodes.rationale: The glove's template index is about 11% longer per palm length than the operator's; the joint angles are the camera's exactly, only the bones are the glove's. Matching the number outright would mean rescaling the template, which this module never does.

nodes.label: cam_open_curl: the camera's open reference is a constant, not learned
nodes.author: Nicholas Kim
nodes.rationale: Curl is a dimensionless ratio, so a straight finger reads about the same on any hand (hands differ by 0.03-0.05). Without pose labels the only way to call a frame open is to ask the glove, which is the claim under suspicion; a constant cannot be poisoned by the data it is judging.
nodes.norm_label: cam_open_curl: the camera's open reference is a constant, not learned

nodes.label: Camera-range guard (--min-camera-range 0.5): whole-hand sweep is the primary curl diagnostic
nodes.author: Nicholas Kim
nodes.rationale: dead_zone_right_ring_20260920_212254.csv: the glove swung 0.86 to 1.97 while the camera's ring curl covered only 0.45, because a gloved ring folding on its own is a shape the tracker does not resolve. Such a run prints no transfer curve and exits 2; the fix is --finger all, not a slower sweep. Coverage needs 5 samples in every 0.1-wide bin.
nodes.norm_label: camera-range guard (--min-camera-range 0.5): whole-hand sweep is the primary curl diagnostic

nodes.label: curl_gates_from_rails: curl_gate carried as a fraction of each finger's learned rail
nodes.author: Nicholas Kim
nodes.rationale: The fit moves every curl value (index open 1.974 to 1.707); left as a constant 1.2 it cost 13 points of camera-use on the ring finger's spread. A constant retuned on one operator's fitted hand would be wrong for the next by exactly the amount the fit removes.
nodes.norm_label: curl_gates_from_rails: curl_gate carried as a fraction of each finger's learned rail

nodes.label: Flexion-fraction normalisation of the thumb vote (frac = (open - curl)/(open - flexed))
nodes.author: Nicholas Kim
nodes.rationale: The two sensors do not share a scale: the glove's straight index reads 1.97 on the template hand, the camera's 1.75. On sync_day1 the raw gate's thumb camera-use went 77.4% to 93.9% when the fit was switched on, mostly the threshold getting looser. 0.20 reproduces the raw gate on unfitted sync_day1 to within 0.1 point. Fingers with span below min_glove_span 0.4 or min_cam_span 0.3 are dropped from the vote.
nodes.norm_label: flexion-fraction normalisation of the thumb vote (frac = (open - curl)/(open - flexed))

nodes.label: How fusion works (src/cam_hand/fusion.py): DOF-split glove + camera fusion, sensors not averaged
nodes.author: Nicholas Kim
nodes.rationale: Averaging a measurement with a guess degrades both. Azimuth is read off the proximal bone because abduction happens at the knuckle; each glove finger chain is rotated about the palm normal at the knuckle so the glove's curl and every bone length survive exactly (the fused hand cannot shrink). The thumb takes its whole direction from the camera. Fusion degrades to glove-only, never to garbage.
nodes.norm_label: how fusion works (src/cam_hand/fusion.py): dof-split glove + camera fusion, sensors not averaged

nodes.label: Glove recorded at full rate with --camera leap (glove_rate_hz, glove_max_gap_ms in meta)
nodes.author: Nicholas Kim
nodes.rationale: At 5 Hz a five-second take is 24 glove frames, which cannot tell a steady stream from one that stopped for three seconds. A mock session at full rate pairs 94% of frames within 50 ms.
nodes.norm_label: glove recorded at full rate with --camera leap (glove_rate_hz, glove_max_gap_ms in meta)

nodes.label: The glove's time lag (about 100 ms left, 450-485 ms right) and pair_by_time glove_lag
nodes.author: Nicholas Kim
nodes.rationale: Measured by cross-correlating index curl over close/open transitions. The pairing stamp is shifted, nothing resampled. auto applies a lag only when at least MIN_LAG_CLIPS = 2 trustworthy estimates agree within MAX_LAG_MAD = 60 ms, with camera curl std and MAD above 0.1 and r >= 0.8; an unmeasured lag is not a zero lag. Held-pose sessions report 'not measurable' and their 649 per-take medians are bit-identical.
nodes.norm_label: the glove's time lag (about 100 ms left, 450-485 ms right) and pair_by_time glove_lag

nodes.label: Leave-one-TAKE-out nearest-centroid classifier (secondary metric)
nodes.author: Nicholas Kim
nodes.rationale: Holding out one sample left the other hand of the same five seconds in the training set, which mostly measured whether a person's two hands look alike.

nodes.label: Per-frame gating of camera-owned DOFs (fusion.GateParams: visible time 300 ms, curl_gate 1.2, view_gate_deg 50, agree_tol_frac 0.20)
nodes.author: Nicholas Kim
nodes.rationale: Ownership does not say whether the camera measured the DOF on this frame: on pinch the camera is right (glove reads its own open palm), on thumbs_up the glove is right. Taking the camera whenever a frame existed made the fused classifier score below glove-only. grab_strength, pinch_strength and confidence are not used as weights. Thresholds are empirical starting points read off one session.

nodes.label: Rail-disagreement override (fusion.RailOverrideParams: on rail, camera trusted, camera flexed, hysteresis 10/5 frames)
nodes.author: Nicholas Kim
nodes.rationale: In all ten pinch takes of sync_day1 the glove index sat exactly on its rail while the camera saw it fold (1.16-1.39), so the fused pinch had a straight index. Not a dead zone: it fails only at the very top of its range, so the override is narrow. Default on, index only. Measured on sync_day1 (59 takes): active on 77.9% of paired pinch frames, 0.00% of fist, index_point, peace, thumbs_up.
nodes.norm_label: rail-disagreement override (fusion.railoverrideparams: on rail, camera trusted, camera flexed, hysteresis 10/5 frames)

nodes.label: Reliability profile (profiles/default.json, reality_glove_nk_2026-09.json): per-hand unreliable and rail fingers
nodes.author: Nicholas Kim
nodes.rationale: Standing knowledge about a glove written down once with the evidence; --profile defaults to auto. With a profile the report prints the fusion both ways, because a mask is a claim that some evidence is worthless. On sync_day2 it moves thumb camera-use 81.7% to 99.5% and the fused classifier 51/59 to 53/59. The right ring stays off the rail-override list until a whole-hand sweep measures it.
nodes.norm_label: reliability profile (profiles/default.json, reality_glove_nk_2026-09.json): per-hand unreliable and rail fingers

nodes.label: Leap takes aligned onto the glove rigidly, without scale (MediaPipe takes keep Umeyama-with-scale)
nodes.author: Nicholas Kim
nodes.rationale: Leap joints are real millimetres and a scale factor would quietly absorb the difference between the hand and the glove's template skeleton.
nodes.norm_label: leap takes aligned onto the glove rigidly, without scale (mediapipe takes keep umeyama-with-scale)

nodes.label: Fitting the glove's template hand to the operator's (src/cam_hand/template_fit.py: measure_hand, fit_template)
nodes.author: Nicholas Kim
nodes.rationale: The glove measures angles, not bone lengths: XR Trainer hangs them on one fixed template (palm 81 mm where the camera measures 96). The fit rescales each offset keeping every rotation, one fixed calibration per hand per session from open-hand camera frames only; refused under MIN_FIT_FRAMES = 200 (sync_day1 has 2482 left, 2204 right). Fused pinch index minus camera goes +0.141 to -0.004 (day 1). The agreement is not an independent validation of the camera.
nodes.norm_label: fitting the glove's template hand to the operator's (src/cam_hand/template_fit.py: measure_hand, fit_template)

nodes.label: Who is allowed to vote in the thumb gate (disputed, overridden, unreliable or un-normalisable fingers excluded)
nodes.author: Nicholas Kim
nodes.rationale: Being on the rail is not on its own a reason to exclude: a first version that excluded every railed finger dropped right-hand peace from 33% to 7%. A rail is suspect only when the camera contradicts it. Below min_usable_fingers = 2 the camera's own geometry decides.
nodes.norm_label: who is allowed to vote in the thumb gate (disputed, overridden, unreliable or un-normalisable fingers excluded)

nodes.label: Two clocks in every recording: wall_time (shared) and the LeapC timestamp (intervals only)
nodes.author: Nicholas Kim
nodes.rationale: wall_time is the only clock the three sensors share and is what fuse_poses pairs on; the LeapC clock has an arbitrary epoch but none of the writer's jitter, so stats.py measures cadence from it. frame_age_us is frame age, not end-to-end latency.
nodes.norm_label: two clocks in every recording: wall_time (shared) and the leapc timestamp (intervals only)

nodes.rationale: Glove run (left hand): 1672 frames in 18.6 s, 98.6 % detection, 0 re-acquisitions, 0.20 mm fingertip jitter at 90 Hz. Bare run: 79.2 % as reported, 1 re-acquisition, 0.54 mm. nodes.label: Path A: simultaneous glove + camera capture
nodes.rationale: Chosen when the gloved hand is reported in 80 %+ of frames, with no more than one re-acquisition per 10 s and jitter within 2x the bare-hand value. The glove supplies flexion; the camera supplies palm pose, spread, thumb and wrist as metric 3D data.

nodes.rationale: IR images confirmed on hardware (384 x 384, 1 bpp per eye); raw .lmt capture confirmed (322 events, reads back). check_setup splits device streaming (FAIL) from hand seen (WARN) because an empty room is not a broken machine. Nothing measured with a hand yet, so Path A vs B was still undecided.

nodes.label: Second gate session (2026-09-17, 13:19 to 13:23): Path A stands, protocol too loose to say more
nodes.rationale: bare right 62 %, glove_right 60 %, glove_both 75/80 %, glove_20cm 94/100 %, glove_35cm 92/87 %, glove_50cm 51 %. Losses are single blocks of 1 to 8 s (edge-on hand, hand at 99 mm, fists), not flicker; the distance labels were not achieved, so there is no evidence beyond about 30 cm. The gate runner needs timed pose prompts, a live height readout and paired bare runs.

nodes.label: A posture calibration fixes a zero, not a frame
nodes.rationale: The open-hand and tmc_neutral calibrations are one rotation each; a change of reference rotation mixes the two TMC angles by pose-dependent amounts, so a zero does not remove cross-talk. On the synthetic example the neutral-posture estimate is off by 4.2 / 6.3 deg MAE with cross-talk slopes 0.075 / 0.088 where the mapped pair is off by 0.9 / 0.6 deg: synthetic numbers that show the mechanism, not this hand.
nodes.norm_label: a posture calibration fixes a zero, not a frame

nodes.label: Calibration / held-out split by trial (the fit sees only calibration samples; the metrics see only held-out samples)

nodes.norm_label: calibration / held-out split by trial (the fit sees only calibration samples; the metrics see only held-out samples)

nodes.label: The thumb TMC mapping d = A R_pm b (palm-to-proximal-frame rotation A, metacarpal long axis b; Levenberg-Marquardt, five parameters)
nodes.rationale: Fitted on the calibration samples from the SVD solution of Wahba's problem; refused when the calibration samples do not span two movement directions (a posture calibration fixes a zero, not a frame). b is a fitted parameter: with a gain or cross-talk in the tracker it moves away from the anatomical axis (19 deg in the synthetic example against 5 deg true), so it is judged by the held-out errors only. A gain or cross-talk is reported, not corrected.
nodes.norm_label: the thumb tmc mapping d = a r_pm b (palm-to-proximal-frame rotation a, metacarpal long axis b; levenberg-marquardt, five parameters)

nodes.label: data_origin and role fields (measured / synthetic / software_cross_check; anatomical_reference / independent_sensor)
nodes.rationale: An instrumented glove declared as anatomical_reference is refused. derived_from_tracker true is accepted only with data_origin and role both software_cross_check: a second calculation from the tracker's own skeleton is a software cross-check, never a reference.

nodes.label: Method: what is compared with what (independent checks vs same-path cross-check; what cannot be checked)
nodes.rationale: FK vs abs26 and bone axis vs bone vector are independent; matrix vs quaternion chain is two code paths over the same data, a cross-check not a measurement. World orientations as the tracker reported them and physical accuracy against the hand cannot be checked from this dataset. capture_time vs timestamp_us intervals agree to 0.326 ms worst (median 0.0019 ms).
nodes.norm_label: method: what is compared with what (independent checks vs same-path cross-check; what cannot be checked)

nodes.label: Clock policy: CLOCK_PREFERENCE timestamp_us, then capture_time, then wall_time, then frame_index_nominal
nodes.rationale: timestamp_us first because it is the camera's own acquisition clock in integer microseconds; capture_time is the same instant on the wall clock; wall_time is the writer and is known to stall. Every fallback is a clock_defect event shown in the HUD and the reports.
nodes.norm_label: clock policy: clock_preference timestamp_us, then capture_time, then wall_time, then frame_index_nominal

nodes.label: Discontinuity policy: segment boundary at id_change or gap > 0.05 s (about 4.5 nominal periods)

nodes.label: Interpolation policy: never by default (hold); interpolate only inside one segment, hold across a boundary
nodes.rationale: The replay shows source frames only: no interpolation, smoothing or anatomical correction by default; across a segment boundary the earlier frame is held and the note says so.
nodes.norm_label: interpolation policy: never by default (hold); interpolate only inside one segment, hold across a boundary

nodes.label: Time-driven playback and the scheduling log (latest source frame at or before media time)

nodes.label: What a change of reference does (corrected 2026-10-24): pose-dependent cross-talk between the two angles, not a fixed offset
nodes.rationale: R_tmc' = D R_tmc with D = R_ref^T R_rest; additive only when D is a pure turn about the abduction axis. Codex's counterexample: a reference at 30 / 20 makes a pose at 30 / 50 read 3.32575 / 25.70535, not 0 / 30. Subtracting a zero measured in one posture does not remove the difference elsewhere. The maths of the mapping is unchanged.

nodes.label: ChatGPT review of day 1 (2026-09-18), adopted
nodes.rationale: Do not conclude the right glove hardware is worse before a reseat and fresh Basic calibration; the thumb gate compares only against trustworthy glove fingers; report fused 95 % vs camera 100 % exactly as it is; the classifier stays secondary; day 2 is the identical protocol plus a separate diagnostic block.

nodes.label: ChatGPT review of day 2 (2026-09-20), adopted
nodes.rationale: Reliability is explicit per hand and finger in a saved profile. A rail override per finger needs repeated static failure on 2+ sessions, stable camera geometry while the glove is wrong, and that finger's own sweep. The rate drop strengthens 'variable transport/software pipeline' without proving Bluetooth. Hold test and sweep must be pose-confirmed and paced.

nodes.label: ChatGPT review of improvements 1 to 3 (2026-09-22) and the follow-up (339 tests)
nodes.rationale: The 77 -> 94 % thumb-use gain was partly a gate-calibration effect (curls compared on two scales): compare normalised flexion fractions instead. Report all three as pipeline improvements, not proof of accuracy. Headline fused classifier unchanged and identical fitted or not: 57/59 (day 1), 53/59 (day 2) with the profile.
nodes.norm_label: chatgpt review of improvements 1 to 3 (2026-09-22) and the follow-up (339 tests)

nodes.label: ChatGPT review of the third session (2026-09-17), all adopted
nodes.rationale: The pose check uses the two sensors under evaluation as arbiter, so it is QC, not ground truth: rejected attempts are kept and each take gets an independent IR still. Pinch check only warns (camera acceptance would bias camera pinch results). Glove recorded at full rate. Minimum for a within-operator conclusion: 5 clean takes x 6 poses x 2 hands on 2 days; the take is the independent sample.

nodes.rationale: 6 poses x 5 takes x 2 hands, one hand at a time. Pairing 17689/17695 within 50 ms, palm fit 3.0 mm median, glove 60 Hz. The right glove under-reads ring and pinky curl; the three fused misses are right-hand takes where glove-owned curl is wrong. Fusion needs per-hand, per-finger reliability logic; glove curl does not automatically dominate.

nodes.label: Day-2 repeat (2026-09-20, sync_day2): 60/60 takes; classifier glove 40/59, camera 59/59, fused 52/59
nodes.rationale: Glove stream worse (median 46 Hz per take, worst gap 142 ms; day 1 was 60 Hz). Left glove repeats day 1 within 0.1; right middle/ring/pinky read open despite recalibration and relax to the open rail within five takes. The per-take IR still caught pinch_right_take1 as a peace hand. Right ring sweep: saturates to open once the finger is only about 40 % bent.
nodes.norm_label: day-2 repeat (2026-09-20, sync_day2): 60/60 takes; classifier glove 40/59, camera 59/59, fused 52/59

nodes.label: Day 3 (2026-09-23 evening, sync_day3): the recalibration's prospective test fails the per-finger criterion
nodes.rationale: 36 takes; glove 30/36, camera 36/36, fused with profile 35/36. The cross-session model helps where day 1's fault reappears and harms where the glove was right (pinch middle .04 -> .77). Verdict: --recalibrate stays OFF and is not stored in the profile; a static model cannot remove a session-dependent calibration error. Next legitimate experiment: a within-session adaptive correction.
nodes.norm_label: day 3 (2026-09-23 evening, sync_day3): the recalibration's prospective test fails the per-finger criterion

nodes.label: The disagreement override (2026-09-25, main 2bc865c+, 441 tests): the fusion no longer follows a drifted glove
nodes.rationale: Prompted by a live left-hand run where the glove drifted open while the trusted camera saw a fist, and the rail-only override needs the glove bit-exact on its rail. RailOverrideParams(mode='disagree'): camera fraction minus glove fraction >= 0.35 for 10 frames, release below 0.20 after 5. Day 2 fused 53/60 -> 59/60 with 0.03 % false fires; both-ways gave 58/60, so camera-more-bent only is the default.
nodes.norm_label: the disagreement override (2026-09-25, main 2bc865c+, 441 tests): the fusion no longer follows a drifted glove

nodes.label: Camera drift anchor (DriftAnchor, --drift-anchor): default OFF, experimental
nodes.rationale: Gains at most one take per day. Pose dependence dominates the glove's error over the timescale of these takes: the right hand's median residual spans 0.4 to 1.05 fraction units across poses while the change within a 5 s take is 0.02 to 0.10.
nodes.norm_label: camera drift anchor (driftanchor, --drift-anchor): default off, experimental

nodes.label: First real Path A session (2026-09-17, 13:44): 193 of 242 glove frames paired; classifier glove 9/10, camera 6/8, fused 5/10
nodes.rationale: Where the camera had a hand it held it: 100 % detection, 0.10 to 0.93 mm jitter, frame age 10 to 12 ms, including a gloved fist. The fused number is not meaningful (one take per pose) but exposes a design gap: fusion takes spread and thumb direction from the camera even when the hand is edge-on, which is when the camera is guessing.

nodes.label: Five code fixes and what they measured (2026-09-23, 392 tests)
nodes.rationale: Reviewed in a fresh ChatGPT chat, its corrections adopted. Rail override on all four fingers changed no classifier row on either day, so the profile stays index only.

nodes.label: Fusion improvements 1 to 3 (merged 2026-09-21, 328 tests): profile by default, glove lag correction, template fit
nodes.rationale: Template fit, day 1 / day 2: fused pinch index curl minus camera +0.141 / +0.139 -> -0.004 / -0.007; fused classifier 55 -> 57/59 and 52 -> 53/59; palm fit on open-palm takes 6.5 / 6.7 -> 4.3 mm. A forced lag shift is never applied: only from a measurement.

nodes.label: Gated fusion (ChatGPT-reviewed design, merged 2026-09-17, 159 tests)
nodes.rationale: A finger's spread comes from the camera only when the glove says it is not curled and the palm faces the lens within 50 deg; the thumb comes from the camera only when the camera agrees with the glove on the other four fingers (median curl disagreement below 0.35). Nothing is dropped: a rejected frame is the glove. Headline is per DOF; the classifier is secondary.

nodes.label: Glove curl creep during a held pose (60 s fist: right index +0.26, about 20 % of the range)
nodes.rationale: The camera stays within +/-0.03 to 0.06 meanwhile. Consistent with viscoelastic creep/hysteresis in soft stretch sensing but not yet located in the capacitive element; fabric/fit and XR Trainer filtering may contribute. On 2026-09-20 only +0.06 to +0.09 in 50 s: session-dependent magnitude.
nodes.norm_label: glove curl creep during a held pose (60 s fist: right index +0.26, about 20 % of the range)

nodes.label: Glove lag behind the camera (right about 455 to 485 ms, left about 100 ms; profile glove_lag_s 0.47 / 0.10)
nodes.rationale: Too large for a BLE connection interval alone, and at a clean 60 Hz packet-rate limits are unlikely; the slow hand changed between days, so it is not a fixed per-glove filter nor an intrinsic glove constant. Applied only to pairing and only from a measurement; it cannot correct creep.
nodes.norm_label: glove lag behind the camera (right about 455 to 485 ms, left about 100 ms; profile glove_lag_s 0.47 / 0.10)

nodes.label: Open issue: the glove's pinch is bit-identical to its open palm (both hands, July and September)
nodes.rationale: Since the glove owns curl, a fused pinch stays open. The left-index sweep of 2026-09-17 showed no general near-extension dead zone: the loss is specific to the pinch shape.
nodes.norm_label: open issue: the glove's pinch is bit-identical to its open palm (both hands, july and september)

nodes.label: Camera-referenced glove recalibration (GloveRecalibration, --recalibrate own|cross): default OFF
nodes.rationale: Ridge regression of the camera fraction on all five glove fractions, trusted frames only, with a rail rule (a finger's own railed readings neither teach nor get corrected; without it pinch poisoned the index). Held-out: day 2 fused 53 -> 59/60. Stays off: the decisive prospective frozen-calibration test failed on day 3 (2026-09-23).
nodes.norm_label: camera-referenced glove recalibration (gloverecalibration, --recalibrate own|cross): default off

nodes.label: Hardened diagnostics, first three runs (2026-09-20, 21:22 to 21:25; 288 tests)
nodes.rationale: hold_test.py and finger_sweep.py merged. Right fist hold: creep only +0.06 to +0.09 in 50 s, lag about 455 ms. With only the right glove connected the glove under-followed a slow relaxation. Paced right ring sweep: the camera did not follow an isolated ring bend (correlation 0.30), so no transfer curve can be read from it.

nodes.label: Runbook: recording Set B (finger flexion) and Set C (sequences)
nodes.rationale: Since 2026-10-12 both sets are recorded with the gloves alone (--camera none): the professor's instruction for these two sets is the data glove, and the Leap Motion camera is for the grasp set only.
nodes.community_name: Protocol Plan: Sets B And C
nodes.norm_label: runbook: recording set b (finger flexion) and set c (sequences)

nodes.label: Amendment 2026-10-12: Sets B and C are recorded with the glove alone
nodes.rationale: The professor's instruction for both sets is the data glove; the Leap Motion camera is the sensor of Set A only, and the research is moving from the camera's keypoints to the glove's joint angles (checked against anatomical limits, then dependencies between joints). The camera beside the gloves becomes an optional comparison run, not part of the hand-in.
nodes.community_name: Protocol Plan: Sets B And C
nodes.norm_label: amendment 2026-10-12: sets b and c are recorded with the glove alone

nodes.label: Amendment 2026-10-13: Set B's bends are checked for speed
nodes.rationale: The professor's text is 'slowly bend the finger until it is fully flexed'; the first glove-only session met every rule with bends of 0.05 to 0.55 s under cues of 4 and 6 s. The quick check now rejects a bend that took under 15 % of a slow cue's time; the straighten is timed and reported, not judged. An acquisition gate, not the definition of a slow bend.
nodes.community_name: Protocol Plan: Sets B And C
nodes.norm_label: amendment 2026-10-13: set b's bends are checked for speed

nodes.label: D5: Sets B and C one hand at a time with the camera as reference (superseded for the hand-in on 2026-10-12)
nodes.rationale: The camera costs nothing extra, verifies each step and gives lag at two speeds (left glove trails by about 0.10 s, right by about 0.47 s). No mirrored two-hand fallback: it changes the geometry the camera sees and the two hands would be cued from one clock.
nodes.community_name: Protocol Plan: Sets B And C
nodes.norm_label: d5: sets b and c one hand at a time with the camera as reference (superseded for the hand-in on 2026-10-12)

nodes.label: D6: Set B timing per cycle (bend 4 s, hold 1 s, straighten 4 s, rest 1 s; index slow 6 s; index fast 1 s, 8 cycles)
nodes.rationale: Every phase of every cycle is a cued event with its own timestamp, so a missed cue, fatigue or creep can be located to the cycle; the protocol JSON states the repetition count so the checker verifies '5 repetitions' rather than assuming it.
nodes.community_name: Protocol Plan: Sets B And C
nodes.norm_label: d6: set b timing per cycle (bend 4 s, hold 1 s, straighten 4 s, rest 1 s; index slow 6 s; index fast 1 s, 8 cycles)

nodes.label: D7: Set C steps held 2.5 s; 3 takes per sequence recorded as three shuffled rounds with a saved seed
nodes.rationale: So the three takes of a sequence are independent repetitions and practice or fatigue cannot be mistaken for a glove effect. The hold window used for checking is the last 1.5 s.
nodes.community_name: Protocol Plan: Sets B And C
nodes.norm_label: d7: set c steps held 2.5 s; 3 takes per sequence recorded as three shuffled rounds with a saved seed

nodes.label: Operator bias: cue-only display during takes; the recorder timestamps every cue and decision
nodes.rationale: One person cues, performs, watches the camera and judges the take, and can unconsciously shape the movement so glove and camera agree or slow down to cover the right glove's lag. The tracker also estimates unseen parts from what it saw before, so a smooth camera trace is not proof the finger was observed.
nodes.community_name: Protocol Plan: Sets B And C
nodes.norm_label: operator bias: cue-only display during takes; the recorder timestamps every cue and decision

nodes.label: Quality rules: acquisition gates kept apart from measured values
nodes.rationale: Acquisition gates are fixed numbers that decide on the spot whether a take is usable; measured values are continuous numbers in the report, and any flagging band comes from that session's warm-up. A fixed threshold is never presented as the definition of a correct movement.
nodes.community_name: Protocol Plan: Sets B And C
nodes.norm_label: quality rules: acquisition gates kept apart from measured values

nodes.label: Protocol files are left byte for byte: a session pins its protocol by sha256
nodes.rationale: The descriptions still say 'gloves on, camera as the reference' after 2026-10-12, but a session whose protocol file no longer matches is read without its cycle counts and windows. Which sensors a session ran is its session.json camera key, never the protocol's description.
nodes.community_name: Protocol Plan: Sets B And C
nodes.norm_label: protocol files are left byte for byte: a session pins its protocol by sha256

nodes.label: The straighten is timed and never judged
nodes.rationale: The glove's reading fell no slower in the sweep's slow openings than in snapped ones, so a bar on the straighten would not tell a slow opening from a fast one. Wording corrected 2026-10-16: the sessions of 2026-10-15 do not show the reading always falls quickly.
nodes.community_name: Protocol Plan: Sets B And C
nodes.norm_label: the straighten is timed and never judged

nodes.label: The glove's thumb is measured by its joint angles in degrees, not by the fingertip distance
nodes.rationale: The fingertip distance barely moves when the thumb bends; the other four fingers keep the fingertip distance.
nodes.community_name: Protocol Plan: Sets B And C
nodes.norm_label: the glove's thumb is measured by its joint angles in degrees, not by the fingertip distance

nodes.label: MyoSuite library
nodes.description: A library on top of MuJoCo (github.com/MyoHub/myosuite), version 3.0.0 here. It ships models and tasks and a Gymnasium wrapper, not recordings of people.

nodes.label: MuJoCo and MyoSuite: what the two links a colleague sent can do for us
nodes.description: A note on what was tried on 7 Nov 2026 with the two simulation tools a colleague suggested as a complement to the Leap Motion research, what came out, and what the tools can and cannot do for the glove-and-camera project. Every MyoSuite number is read from the model by the hand-limits script; nothing is quoted from a web page.
nodes.norm_label: mujoco and myosuite: what the two links a colleague sent can do for us

nodes.label: MuJoCo physics engine
nodes.description: A physics engine (mujoco.org): rigid bodies, joints with limits, contacts, tendons and muscle actuators, with Python bindings; version 4.0.0 here. It is the engine, not a hand.

nodes.label: Gates: what MuJoCo and MyoSuite can do for us
nodes.description: Acceptance gates M1 to M5 for finding out what the two simulation tools a colleague sent can do for the glove-and-camera project: install them in a repo-local venv, load MyoSuite's musculoskeletal hand with MuJoCo, dump every hand joint's biomechanical range in degrees, set those ranges beside Paper 3's Table 5 ranges and the glove's measured spans under the repo's 24 angle names, and write a short note. No hardware is run; nothing is committed.
nodes.norm_label: gates: what mujoco and myosuite can do for us

nodes.label: Gate P6: the 50 glove poses print as one PDF with a MyoHand render pair beside every pose
nodes.description: Added 11 Nov 2026. The PDF is built from the existing renders by the MyoSuite venv; every page was looked at (11 pages, no row cut, 100 pictures).
nodes.norm_label: gate p6: the 50 glove poses print as one pdf with a myohand render pair beside every pose

nodes.label: .venv-myo: the repo-local MyoSuite venv
nodes.description: Both tools installed and ran on a Windows 11 machine with Python 3.14; no Linux, no GPU and no PyTorch were needed. The hand compiles and 100 simulation steps leave every joint finite.

nodes.label: Gate M2: the joint-limit CSV has one row per hand joint and the comparison CSV has exactly the repo's 24 angle names in order
nodes.description: Each of the 24 angles carries the matched MyoSuite joint, its range in degrees, Paper 3's Table 5 range and hyperextension as printed, and the glove's measured span from the pilot audit, with an empty cell wherever a source has nothing for that angle.
nodes.norm_label: gate m2: the joint-limit csv has one row per hand joint and the comparison csv has exactly the repo's 24 angle names in order

nodes.label: MyoHand jnt_range: the model's joint limit table
nodes.description: Every finger MCP, PIP and DIP flexion runs 0 to 90 degrees with no hyperextension, and every MCP abduction is plus or minus 15 degrees. The thumb allows 45 degrees of TMC flexion and 40 of extension, 29 of TMC adduction and 45 of abduction, 45 of MCP flexion and 40 of extension, 75 of IP flexion and 25 of extension.
nodes.norm_label: myohand jnt_range: the model's joint limit table

nodes.label: MyoHand sign conventions, measured by driving each joint to its minimum and maximum
nodes.description: For the four thumb joints the negative end brings the thumb toward the palm, so negative is flexion (and adduction for the CMC abduction joint); for the finger joints the positive end is flexion and abduction has no fixed sign.
nodes.norm_label: myohand sign conventions, measured by driving each joint to its minimum and maximum

nodes.label: Mapping from the 24 angles to MyoHand qpos (zero posture and the thumb's sign flips)
nodes.description: Has to be built first; it is the first concrete task on the path, followed by one recorded fist replayed through it.
nodes.norm_label: mapping from the 24 angles to myohand qpos (zero posture and the thumb's sign flips)

nodes.label: Finding: the glove's own exports look clamped at round-number ceilings
nodes.description: Index PIP stops at exactly 90.00, middle and ring PIP at exactly 100.00, index MCP at 89.76. Ceilings like these are software limits in the glove's export, not joints stopping; worth confirming with StretchSense before any limit comparison uses glove maxima.
nodes.norm_label: finding: the glove's own exports look clamped at round-number ceilings

nodes.label: MyoHand has no finger CMC joints: the palm arc stays unmeasured and unsimulated
nodes.description: Its four finger metacarpals are fixed in the palm, exactly as LeapC's rigid palm is, so the simulation cannot fill the gaps the camera leaves.
nodes.norm_label: myohand has no finger cmc joints: the palm arc stays unmeasured and unsimulated

nodes.label: Finding: the two limit tables disagree where it matters for a fist
nodes.description: MyoHand caps PIP at 90 degrees for every finger; the literature ranges in Paper 3 run 110 to 135, and the glove itself reported 100 on the middle and ring PIP during the fist take. Clamping to MyoHand would cut real flexion.
nodes.norm_label: finding: the two limit tables disagree where it matters for a fist

nodes.label: Finding: the thumb cannot be compared cell by cell
nodes.description: MyoHand's thumb axes, like the camera's, are not the paper's TMC axes, and its ranges are two-sided around a zero posture the paper does not define.
nodes.norm_label: finding: the thumb cannot be compared cell by cell

nodes.label: MyoSuite gives no human data
nodes.description: MyoSuite ships models and tasks, not recordings of people; the comparison datasets listed in the project's comparison data sources note remain the only human references.

nodes.label: MyoHand: musculoskeletal right hand with 23 joints and 39 muscle actuators
nodes.description: MyoSuite's hand model, converted from two OpenSim models. Its muscles are tendon-driven (FDP, FDS, EDC and the intrinsics).
nodes.norm_label: myohand: musculoskeletal right hand with 23 joints and 39 muscle actuators

nodes.label: Finding: MyoHand allows no MCP hyperextension
nodes.description: Paper 3 allows 30 to 40 degrees, and the open-palm take needs some of it.
nodes.norm_label: finding: myohand allows no mcp hyperextension

nodes.label: MyoSuite's 24 myoHand reinforcement-learning tasks
nodes.description: Pose reaching, key turn, pen twirl, baoding balls and die reorientation. myoHandPoseFixed-v0 builds, resets and steps in 1.4 s here (observation 108 values, action 39 muscles).

nodes.label: myo_sim package: composes and compiles the hand model

nodes.label: Drive the simulated hand with captured angles
nodes.rationale: MyoHand's 23 joints are set directly, so a recorded take's angles can be written into the model frame by frame. nodes.rationale: They are a model's jnt_range and for the fingers they are round numbers. Paper 3's literature ranges give PIP 110 to 135 degrees and 30 to 40 degrees of MCP hyperextension, so a filter built from MyoHand would clip a real fist. Nothing here checks either table against anatomy sources.

nodes.label: Next step: decide with the colleague which table the anatomical filter clamps to
nodes.rationale: The evidence points to Paper 3's Table 5 for the limits (it is the literature table, it is already in the repo, and MyoHand's finger limits are tighter than real fists) and to MyoHand for what a table cannot do: driving a simulated hand with the captured angles to render the replay, check self-penetration and measure fingertip error.

nodes.label: Why one plane: poses limited to what the glove senses
nodes.rationale: The glove senses flexion. It has no sensor for finger spread and none for the wrist, and its flexion never reads below 0, so it cannot show hyperextension. So every pose keeps the fingers side by side, the wrist straight and the thumb in its own bending plane, and uses no hyperextension state. A pose that needed spread, wrist motion or thumb opposition would be measured by the camera only, which is the camera catalogue's job.
nodes.norm_label: why one plane: poses limited to what the glove senses

nodes.label: Single-plane rule: each digit moves only in its own flexion-extension plane
nodes.rationale: Every pose has no finger spread, no wrist deviation and no thumb opposition out of the palm plane, because flexion in each digit's own plane is what the glove senses.
nodes.norm_label: single-plane rule: each digit moves only in its own flexion-extension plane

nodes.label: Finding 1: real-time playback (acceptance at least 30 rendered updates per second in three trials, gate K9)
nodes.rationale: Reproduce first (three TkAgg trials at 1x on p3_circular_power take 1, 449 frames, 4.989 s), then profile one tick on the real path before changing anything; fix the measured costs only (reuse reconstructions, render only changed text, redraw only what moved, blit only the dirty region). Rendered updates are counted separately from timer ticks and skipped frames. The media clock is not touched; every source frame stays reachable by stepping.

nodes.label: Finding 2: interpolation through invalid tracking (a status-0 line between selected frames is a discontinuity; gate K2)
nodes.rationale: load_recording passes those positions to find_segments, which cuts the segment there; pose_at in interpolate mode then holds the earlier frame and names invalid_status as the reason. Invalid lines before the first or after the last selected frame cut nothing. Codex's own synthetic file is re-run after the fix.

nodes.label: Finding 4: calibration kind ('openhand' | 'neutral') and hand on tmc_estimate.Calibration
nodes.rationale: Outputs are named by the kind (*_est_openhand or *_est_neutral); from_json infers kind from the writers' provenance prefixes for older files and rejects anything else; a calibration of another session or another hand is not applied, with the reason shown. The coverage table distinguishes calculated tracker coordinates, open-hand-relative estimates, neutral-posture-relative estimates and unavailable anatomical coordinates; the per-frame export has four estimate columns.

nodes.label: T_TMC_aa: thumb trapeziometacarpal abduction (specification)
nodes.rationale: Canonical sign: positive palmar, out of the plane of the palm. A direction of the metacarpal needs both angles, so the two TMC angles are measured and compared together.

nodes.label: T_TMC_fe: thumb trapeziometacarpal flexion (specification)
nodes.rationale: Canonical sign: positive when the metacarpal head moves toward the ulnar side across the palm. The tracker supplies the thumb metacarpal's orientation against the rigid palm (moves up to 40.25 deg in a recording) and nothing anatomical. Accuracy check: mapping fitted on calibration trials only, metrics on held-out trials, with no threshold applied.

nodes.label: Canonical convention (e3 along the metacarpal toward its head, e2 the palmar normal, e1 = e2 x e3)
nodes.rationale: Every reference value is converted on import: thumb flexion positive ulnar about e2, thumb abduction positive palmar about e1, finger CMC flexion positive palmar. A declared opposite sign is flipped, radians are converted, and the declared rotation order is used to turn the two thumb angles into the metacarpal's direction and back.
nodes.norm_label: canonical convention (e3 along the metacarpal toward its head, e2 the palmar normal, e1 = e2 x e3)

nodes.label: Sample matching on the tracker clock (never across a gap, an identity change or an invalid-status line)
nodes.rationale: An instant is matched to the pose interpolated between the two bracketing frames of one segment (replay_core.pose_at); a hold to the chordal mean of its frames, which must lie in one segment. The tracker quantity is the bone against the palm, R_pm = R_palm^T R_bone.
nodes.norm_label: sample matching on the tracker clock (never across a gap, an identity change or an invalid-status line)

nodes.label: Optional goniometer reading of the posture (radial abduction and palmar abduction; --goniometer)
nodes.source_location: What a goniometer reading would add
nodes.rationale: Makes the posture's own error a measured quantity instead of an assumption of zero, and would later allow a one-point scale check. It does not add the ISB neutral, the tracker's own error on the thumb, or the mapping's scale and cross-talk; those need an independent sensor (Paper 3 used a Cyberglove).
nodes.norm_label: optional goniometer reading of the posture (radial abduction and palmar abduction; --goniometer)

nodes.label: Posture tmc_neutral_v1: hand flat, fingers straight and together, thumb straight against the side of the index in the plane of the palm
nodes.rationale: A calibration take replaces the incidental open hand with a posture that is defined before it is held, held on purpose, held still, and held again, so the zero is a stated posture and its repeatability is measured. It does not by itself validate the estimate. The definition is written into every take's sidecar (POSE_DEFINITION) so the file and the page cannot drift apart.
nodes.norm_label: posture tmc_neutral_v1: hand flat, fingers straight and together, thumb straight against the side of the index in the plane of the palm

nodes.label: What to check first (canonical convention signs, the fit never sees a held-out sample, no interpolation across a discontinuity, scope of a mapping, known limits)
nodes.rationale: Known limits: the order of a reference's two angles cannot be checked from data (0.12 deg); b is a fitted parameter that can absorb gain (19 deg against 5 deg true in the example); the sync taps' distance thresholds are untested on real hands; the identifiability conditions are chosen here, not accuracy thresholds.
nodes.norm_label: what to check first (canonical convention signs, the fit never sees a held-out sample, no interpolation across a discontinuity, scope of a mapping, known limits)

nodes.label: Correction plan after Codex's independent verification (2026-10-24)
nodes.rationale: Every verification output of this correction goes to results/replay_fidelity/codex_corrections_20261024/; nothing in the dataset, in the earlier replay_fidelity run or in other sessions' uncommitted files is overwritten.
nodes.norm_label: correction plan after codex's independent verification (2026-10-24)

nodes.label: Protocol: the thumb TMC calibration take tmc_neutral (written 2026-10-23; not yet run on the camera)
nodes.rationale: A recording-protocol addition to the thumb TMC estimate; it changes nothing in that estimate's maths. The mock path and the tests are the only runs so far.
nodes.norm_label: protocol: the thumb tmc calibration take tmc_neutral (written 2026-10-23; not yet run on the camera)

nodes.label: Finding 3: thumb-coordinate wording (no fixed per-angle offset; posture-dependent cross-talk)
nodes.rationale: The estimate is a tracker-relative coordinate pair referred to a chosen reference orientation R_rest and decomposed abduction-first. Changing the reference is an additive constant only for a pure turn about the abduction axis; in general both components change by posture-dependent amounts, so the difference from Paper 3's anatomical TMC angles is posture-dependent and unknown, not a zero offset to subtract. The maths is not changed; every sentence claiming a fixed per-angle offset is replaced, Codex's counterexample and a positive control become a test, and a test scans docs and code for the old claim.
nodes.norm_label: finding 3: thumb-coordinate wording (no fixed per-angle offset; posture-dependent cross-talk)

nodes.label: The tracker's PALM joint as a proxy for the trapezium
nodes.rationale: Using the rigid PALM frame for the carpus assumes the trapezium keeps a fixed orientation in it; that holds to within the motion of the second and third CMC joints (5 deg each in Paper 3) plus whatever the palm fit does when the ring and little metacarpals arch. Neither is measured. The fixed part of the proxy is exactly what the mapping fits (A); the changing part shows up in the held-out errors.
nodes.norm_label: the tracker's palm joint as a proxy for the trapezium

nodes.label: Rotation order is part of the coordinate's definition (Paper 3 abduction then flexion; ISB flexion then abduction then axial rotation)
nodes.rationale: With both angles non zero the two orders give different pairs for one direction (30 / 20 abduction-first reads 31.57 / 17.23 flexion-first). The capture declares the order and is refused when it is missing; the comparison cannot detect a wrongly declared order (it moves the held-out errors by 0.12 deg in the test), so it must come from the device's documentation.
nodes.norm_label: rotation order is part of the coordinate's definition (paper 3 abduction then flexion; isb flexion then abduction then axial rotation)

nodes.label: Thumb TMC observable but unvalidated (the tracker reports its motion; how accurately is unknown)
nodes.rationale: Against a calibration posture the metacarpal gives a tracker-relative pair, the unvalidated estimate T_TMC_*_est_openhand / T_TMC_*_est_neutral. The trapezium is not tracked, there are no palpated landmarks, and no independent device recorded these sessions, so nothing ties that pair to Paper 3's or the ISB's TMC angles.
nodes.norm_label: thumb tmc observable but unvalidated (the tracker reports its motion; how accurately is unknown)

nodes.label: Assumption A5: LeapC's rigid PALM joint stands for the carpus (the trapezium is not tracked)
nodes.rationale: The thumb metacarpal bone's base and head are the model's, not palpated, so neither the Cooney/ISB trapezium frame nor Cheze's functional axes can be built from a recording.
nodes.norm_label: assumption a5: leapc's rigid palm joint stands for the carpus (the trapezium is not tracked)

nodes.label: Clinical thumb goniometry starting position as the stand-in zero (radial and palmar abduction both zero)
nodes.rationale: A camera-only setup has no trapezium or palpated landmarks, so the neutral cannot be fixed by bone frames; what it can fix is a posture. This one is reproducible by an operator without a second person and is the reference clinical measurements of the thumb start from. The offset between it and the ISB bone-aligned neutral is unknown and stays unknown here.
nodes.norm_label: clinical thumb goniometry starting position as the stand-in zero (radial and palmar abduction both zero)

nodes.label: Every number against this zero is written under *_est_neutral, never under a Paper 3 name
nodes.norm_label: every number against this zero is written under *_est_neutral, never under a paper 3 name

nodes.label: The hold: duration from the frames' own camera clock (hold_s; skipped under 2 s or 20 frames)
nodes.rationale: The recorder commands 5 s, but the duration that counts is the span of timestamp_us; the commanded wall-clock hold is kept as hold_commanded_s for cross-checking, never used in its place. The 2 s is the grasp protocol's static interval, the 20 frames the open-hand calibration's own minimum.
nodes.norm_label: the hold: duration from the frames' own camera clock (hold_s; skipped under 2 s or 20 frames)

nodes.label: Incidental open-hand zero R_rest (across-transition agreement median 4.4, p90 7.8, max 20.0 degrees on 2026-10-23)
nodes.rationale: Today R_rest is the open hand the participant happened to hold before each transition cue; nobody defined the thumb's position in it, so the estimate differs from any anatomical TMC angle by an unmeasured change of reference (assumption A3), which is pose-dependent and mixes the two angles (corrected 2026-10-24). The across-transition agreement is its floor uncertainty.
nodes.norm_label: incidental open-hand zero r_rest (across-transition agreement median 4.4, p90 7.8, max 20.0 degrees on 2026-10-23)

nodes.label: Project rules for a protocol step: posted in the xr-training ChatGPT thread first; names its hardware setup; one action per step; durations from timestamps
nodes.norm_label: project rules for a protocol step: posted in the xr-training chatgpt thread first; names its hardware setup; one action per step; durations from timestamps

nodes.label: Three independent takes per session; across-take agreement; re-record when agreement_max_deg is above 4.4 degrees
nodes.rationale: The hand comes off the posture and is made again before each take, so the takes are independent makings. One chordal mean per take and the chordal mean of those as R_rest. Three is the smallest number that gives a worst take and a median. 4.4 degrees is the open-hand calibration's median across-transition agreement on 2026-10-23: a posture made on purpose three times should agree at least as well as incidental open hands did. Every folder is kept.
nodes.norm_label: three independent takes per session; across-take agreement; re-record when agreement_max_deg is above 4.4 degrees
